title: No recovery on Auto Hide Cursor

judgment.rationale: The original report already provided clear reproduction steps and video evidence. The author’s follow-up now narrows the case to a physical Snapdragon Surface touchpad and identifies the likely simulated-input filtering branch, making a maintainer reproduction and trace the correct next step.
evidence: Auto Hide Cursor is enabled and the cursor remains hidden after movement until the utility is disabled.
The original report includes PowerToys v0.101.2572, Windows 11 25H2, OS build 26200.9457, and a video.
The author confirmed the issue on a physical Snapdragon Surface Laptop using its touchpad.
Touchpad clicking and scrolling do not restore the cursor.
The author pointed to AutoHideCursorWorker.cpp line 291 and suspected simulated cursor actions are ignored.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce on a touchpad-equipped Snapdragon device and trace injected-input filtering, movement classification, and cursor restoration before selecting a fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: The new evidence makes the simulated-input branch a strong hypothesis, but the maintainer still needs to confirm whether the hook flags are the actual failing discriminator and whether changing them affects intentional automation input.

issue_context.summary: Auto Hide Cursor does not restore visibility after touchpad movement on a Snapdragon Surface Laptop, and disabling the utility is the only known recovery.
known_information: The report targets Auto Hide Cursor on PowerToys v0.101.2572.
The reporter supplied a video and clear hide-then-move steps.
The author confirmed the issue on a physical Snapdragon Surface Laptop using a touchpad.
Clicking and scrolling also fail to restore the cursor.
The author suspects the worker ignores simulated cursor actions at AutoHideCursorWorker.cpp line 291.
The issue was updated by the author on 2026-09-24.
inferences: Touchpad-generated movement may be marked as injected or otherwise filtered before AutoHideCursorState::OnMouseInput can return Show.
The failure may instead occur in cursor restoration after the state transition, so both branches need tracing.
issue_context.analysis: The author supplied discriminating hardware and input-path evidence, so another generic information request would be wasteful. A controlled touchpad reproduction with hook flags and restore results recorded can confirm or reject the proposed branch.
initial_investigation: Re-read the complete issue and all three comments, including the author’s source-line hypothesis.
Retained the earlier source observations that AutoHideCursorState::OnMouseInput should show on intentional movement and SystemCursorHider restores system cursors.
Updated the triage freshness to cover the author’s 2026-09-24 response.

reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys v0.101.2572 or newer current build
prerequisites: Physical Snapdragon Surface Laptop or comparable touchpad device
Tracing or logging for low-level mouse-hook flags and cursor restoration
steps: Trigger hiding by typing and wait until the cursor disappears.
Move the touchpad pointer beyond the intentional movement threshold.
Try touchpad left click, right click, and scrolling.
Repeat after triggering hide through the idle timer.
Disable Auto Hide Cursor and confirm that the cursor is restored.
reproduce.expected_result: Intentional touchpad movement, click, or scrolling restores the cursor without disabling the utility.
setup_requirements: Record whether the low-level hook marks touchpad events as LLMHF_INJECTED or LLMHF_LOWER_IL_INJECTED.
Record whether SystemCursorHider::Restore and RestoreSystemCursors succeed.
